国内生产总值(GDP)是指按市场价格计算的一个国家（或地区）所有常住单位在一定时: Gross domestic product (GDP) refers to the final results of the production activities of all resident units of a country (or region) during a given period, valued at market prices. GDP has three manifestations: the value form, the income form, and the product form. In value terms, it is the difference between the value of all goods and services produced by all resident units during a given period and the value of all non-fixed-asset goods and services consumed in the same period, i.e. the sum of the value added of all resident units. In income terms, it is the sum of primary incomes created by all resident units during a given period and distributed to resident and non-resident units. In product terms, it is the sum of the value of goods and services finally used by all resident units during a given period plus net exports of goods and services. In practice, GDP is compiled using three methods: the production approach, the income approach, and the expenditure approach, each of which reflects GDP and its composition from a different perspective.

(1) Coverage: the output value of completed works is the entire value self-completed on an individual project completed during the reporting period, from the start to the completion of the project, covering: (i) for individual projects with construction spanning more than one year, the output value of completed works should include the entire self-completed value of the project from start to completion; (ii) for some large individual projects, such as large plant buildings, high-grade hotels, various pipelines, highways and railways, which can be constructed by span, storey or section and, as stipulated in the contract, can be delivered for use separately, the output value of completed works may be calculated separately. The output value of completed works excludes the value of production and services provided to outside units by affiliated auxiliary enterprises or other internally accounted units. (2) Statistical basis: the output value of completed works may be counted for a contracted project only when both of the following conditions are met simultaneously: (i) the content of the individual project stipulated in the contract has been fully completed and the handover conditions specified in the design have been met; (ii) it has passed inspection and acceptance by the relevant authorities. It is one of the internationally used leading indices for monitoring macroeconomic trends and has strong predictive and early-warning value. The PMI is a composite index calculated as the weighted sum of five diffusion indices (sub-indices). The five sub-indices and their weights are determined according to the degree to which they lead the economy. They are: the new orders index, weight 30%; the production index, weight 25%; the employment index, weight 20%; the supplier delivery time index, weight 15%; and the raw materials inventory index, weight 10%. Of these, the supplier delivery time index is an inverse index and is reversed when the composite PMI is calculated. A level of 50% is generally taken as the threshold between economic expansion and contraction: a PMI above 50% indicates expansion in manufacturing, while a level below 50% indicates contraction.

Compared with previous base periods, the eight major categories changed significantly in this round: "food" and "tobacco and liquor" were merged into "food, tobacco and liquor"; "health care and personal articles" was split into "household articles and services", "health care" and "other articles and services"; "recreation, education, cultural articles and services" was split into "education, culture and recreation" and "other articles and services"; and "household facilities, articles and services" was split into "household articles and services" and "other articles and services". In addition, the content of "food" changed: in previous base periods "food" was a major category including grain, meat and poultry, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits, aquatic products, tea and beverages, and dining out; in this round "food" is a sub-category under "food, tobacco and liquor", covering only grain, livestock meat, poultry, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits and aquatic products, and no longer including "tea and beverages" or "dining out".
From January 2021, the CPI has been compiled and released with 2020 as the base period. This round still comprises eight major categories: food, tobacco and liquor; clothing; residence; household articles and services; transport and communication; education, culture and recreation; health care; and other articles and services, with basic categories increased to 268.

GDP has three forms of expression: the value form, the income form and the product form. In the value form, it is the difference between the value of all goods and services produced by all resident units in a given period and the value of all non-fixed-asset goods and services used as inputs in the same period, i.e. the sum of the value added of all resident units. In the income form, it is the sum of the primary incomes created by all resident units in a given period and distributed to resident and non-resident units. In the product form, it is the value of goods and services finally used by all resident units in a given period plus net exports of goods and services. In practice, GDP is compiled by three methods: the production approach, the income approach and the expenditure approach, each reflecting GDP and its composition from a different perspective. Calculated at current prices. For a region, it is referred to as gross regional product or regional GDP.
